newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks see Dow fallout, close lower.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks see Dow fallout, close lower.

text.p: Mexican stocks could not escape the wave of selling that washed over Wall Street on Friday, closing lower on a day where the only bright spot was an initial public offering by broadcaster TV Azteca.
The leading IPC stock index fell below the key 5,000 point support level to 4,956.61 points, off 58 points or almost 1.16 percent on the day.
Mexican stocks held up well considering the massive sell-off on Wall Street, where stocks suffered their biggest point loss since the 1987 stock market crash.
The Dow Jones industrial average tumbled 247.37 points, or 3.1 percent, at 7,694.66, marking its second-biggest point drop ever.
"In a sense, I'm surprised the market here held up that well. The profit-taking was moderate and in that sense, this is a positive," said Felix Boni, head of analysis at ING Barings in Mexico City.
"There is still interest in Mexico. Maybe investors aren't coming in as fast right now, but most aren't leaving either, they are willing to hang on awhile," he added.
In the broad market, declining shares outpaced gainers by a 32-52 margin on very thin volume of 56.22 million shares, of which more than a third were from the Azteca IPO.

Azteca, Mexico's second-largest broadcaster, issued shares on both the Mexican and New York stock exchanges. Its ordinary shares in Mexico rose from an initial offer price of 35.43 pesos ($4.56) to 36.80 pesos ($4.74).
On Wall Street, Azteca's American Depositary Shares rose 15/16 to 19-3/16.
Market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) fell 28 centavos (3.6 cents) to 19.82 pesos ($2.55) and 13/16 to 51-5/16 in New York.
